description: Parity cases of the names rule of a written text (design D20): the same cases are played against tools/sensitive_names.py (tests/sensitive_names/test_parite_texte.py) and against contract/src/texte.ts (contract/test/texte.test.ts). Invented names only.

cases.name: unicode case: the sharp s in the same case
unicode case: the capital sharp s meets the sharp s (simple case folding)
unicode case: no multi-character folding, SS is not the sharp s
a CRLF inside the text does not hide a name
a lone carriage return before a name: the name is still a whole word
a whole name
cases.text: the review by Zorglub Martin is late

cases.name: case ignored for a long name
a name stuck to a letter does not match
a name stuck after a letter does not match
a name stuck to an underscore does not match
a three-character name keeps its case
a three-character name in another case does not match
an acronym keeps its case
an acronym in lower case does not match
a name that starts with a letter and holds a symbol
that name stuck to a letter does not match
a name that starts with a symbol
a name that starts with a symbol, after a letter
no name
cases.text: the lead time rose in the second quarter

cases.name: audit 629 L3-06: a no-break space inside a name does not hide it
audit 629 L3-06: a narrow no-break space and an ideographic space do not hide a name
cases.text: asked Zorglub Martin and Quentin　Duval

cases.name: audit 629 L3-06: a zero-width space inside a name does not hide it
audit 629 L3-06: a soft hyphen and a word joiner inside a name do not hide it
audit 629 L3-06: a decomposed accent (NFD) meets a composed name (NFC)
audit 629 L3-06: a full-width letter is read as its plain letter
audit 629 L3-06: several spaces and a tab between the words of a name
audit 629 L3-06: a non-breaking hyphen meets the hyphen of a name
audit 629 L3-06: a minus sign meets the hyphen of a name
audit 629 L3-06: a zero-width space after a name, then a letter: the raw text keeps the word boundary, so the name is refused
audit 629 L3-06: a letter, then a zero-width space, then a name: the raw text keeps the word boundary, so the name is refused
audit 629 L3-06: a zero-width space between two words of no name stays no name
